Always consume log_level arg in ProgressBarOperation.Run Fix inconsistent handling of the log_level keyword argument in ProgressBarOperation.Run(). This method was indeed passing the log_level keyword argument to its callback in certain cases, but not in others. In particular, when running cros deploy with redirected stdout (isatty() returning False) Run() passed the log_level argument to its callback. This caused failures to run cros deploy when redirecting its output to a file, for example. This commit fixes the issue by changing the Run() method so that it always consumes the log_level argument and uses it to set the log level under which the callback function is ran. BUG=chromium:623999 TEST=lib/operation_unittest cli/deploy_unittest Change-Id: I846d3868d3274d01d017a4b80b84eb91345586b0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/445787 Commit-Ready: Matteo Franchin <matteo.franchin@arm.com> Tested-by: Matteo Franchin <matteo.franchin@arm.com> Reviewed-by: Chris Sosa <sosa@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: google: vpd: Ignore attributes with invalid name. The VPD entries should be named by only alphabets, digits, or underline character. Previously the user land tool 'vpd' didn't check key names and may create entries like "S/N", which would lead to problems when exporting VPD entries as /sys attributes. The VPD specification has been changed to support only [a-zA-Z0-9_]+. For devices already shipped with invalid names, we should ignore those attributes (still accessible via command "vpd -l"). BUG=chromium:698362 TEST=Add a VPD entry with invalid name (vpd -s S/N=Data), reboot, and check attributes (ls -l /sys/firmware/vpd/ro). The 'S/N' entry is not created. cr50: change DEV to DBG in debug images version strings There are two types of signing of CR50 images - prod and dev. Designating images built with CR50_DEV variable set in the environment as DEV is confusing, as this has nothing to do with the signing type (dev vs prod), and is in fact indicating an image with many debug features enabled. This patch changes the string to "DBG". Make umpire and finalize_bundle compute toolkit MD5SUM correctly Currently Umpire and finalize_bundle compute toolkit MD5SUM in two different wrong ways. Umpire mistakenly only uses the prefix of MD5 of install_factory_toolkit.run, while finalize_bundle generates MD5SUM from factory test image. This makes the checksum in fresh net installed DUT different to the one in Umpire, and increase the probability of collision. Make both of them use full MD5 checksum of install_factory_toolkit.run BUG=b:31693381 TEST=manually 1. create a bundle with finalize_bundle 2. check if dev_image/factory/MD5SUM in state.gz is correct 3. import the bundle 4. check if /docker_shared/umpire/default/toolkits/.../MD5SUM is correct Change-Id: I767022c2b8b9c0b4ef906af25142eb23583001fc Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/449636 Commit-Ready: Youcheng Syu <youcheng@chromium.org> Tested-by: Youcheng Syu <youcheng@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mao Huang <littlecvr@chromium.org>
